title: coordinated-tenant-upgrade-and-backout-matrix
author: Priya Raman
body:
Summary

This playbook defines a coordinated tenant upgrade pattern for Redwood Private deployments and an explicit backout (rollback) matrix. It is intended for field operations, SREs, and on-prem engineers who run upgrades that touch model artifacts, runtime images, KV cache formats, or GPU driver/firmware. The approach favors reproducibility, minimal blast radius, and clear operator decision points.

Goals

- Enable deterministic, low-risk upgrades across N tenants sharing a control plane or host cluster.
- Provide crisp rollback triggers, owners, and expected recovery targets (RTO/RPO).
- Standardize pre-checks, canary success criteria, and automated verification steps.

When to use this guide

Use this playbook when any of the following change types are planned for a private deployment:
1) Runtime binary or container image updates (inference runtime, router, sidecars)
2) Model hot-swap or quantization variant swaps that change KV cache semantics
3) Persistent-state or schema migrations (e.g., embedding-store format)
4) Kernel/driver or GPU firmware updates that may affect latency characteristics

Prerequisites

- Release artifact is signed and present in the customer-approved registry.
- Control-plane and agent components are at or above minimum compatibility versions: runtime >= 3.4.0, agent >= 1.12.0.
- Nightly snapshot and a validated rollback image exist in the internal registry.
- Acceptance test harness (see /confluence/eng-private-deployments/day-2-ops/post-installation-telemetry-and-acceptance-checklist-2026) is runnable against a canary tenant.
- Slack / PagerDuty on-call contact for SRE and Field-Ops have been notified at T-48h.

Owner & Responsibilities

- Release owner: Release Engineer (owner: @re-release-engineering) — coordinates artifacts and gating.
- Canary operator: Field Operations engineer — owns canary execution and initial verification.
- Rollback owner: SRE lead on-call — makes rollback authorization calls when thresholds cross.
- Customer comms: Customer Success / Account Manager — coordinates scheduled downtime/maintenance window notices.

Tenant Risk Grouping (recommended)

Group tenants by risk profile for staged rollouts:
- Group A (low-risk): staging, dev, non-production; high tolerance for transient errors.
- Group B (medium-risk): small production customers with no strict SLA, can tolerate brief degradation.
- Group C (high-risk): enterprise customers with strict SLAs and data isolation requirements.

Suggested staging order: Group A -> Group B -> Group C (with pause and evaluation between groups).

Canary Strategy and Success Criteria

- Canary size: 1–3 tenants from Group B (or 5% of total traffic for large clusters).
- Traffic shaping: direct 100% of selected tenants' traffic to the new runtime; do not split traffic within a tenant for stateful model-swap operations.
- Acceptance checks (must pass all):
  - API error rate < 0.5% over 10 minute window
  - 95th token-latency delta compared to baseline < +25% for text-generation paths
  - Model output quality sanity: 5 pre-defined prompt sets (see prompt-sets and eval harness) must pass regression thresholds
  - KV cache warmup success: measured cache hit-rate >= 70% within first 30 minutes of warmup for LRU-dominated workloads

Backout Matrix (table)

| Failure Mode | Immediate Operator Action | Rollback Trigger (boolean) | Expected RTO | Owner |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Increased 95th latency > +50% for > 10m | Pause rollout, scale down new pods, switch canary traffic to previous image | true | 15m | Canary operator / SRE on-call |
| API error rate > 2% | Disable new route, create incident, begin rollback | true | 10m | SRE on-call |
| Persistent model correctness regressions (failing evals) | Stop rollout, retain metrics, notify product & research | true | 30m | Release owner + Applied ML reviewer |
| KV cache corruption detected (data loss or checksum mismatch) | Immediate stop, isolate impacted hosts, restore from last healthy snapshot | true | 60m | Release owner + Storage lead |
| Transient pod crash-loop (single host) | Reprovision node, re-run canary; do not auto-rollback unless >3 nodes affected | false (manual review) | 45m | Field Ops |
| Driver/firmware side-effects (GPU reboots) | Halt all upgrades, do not roll forward; initiate emergency patch process | true | 120m | Platform SRE |

Operational playbook (step-by-step)

1) T-72h: Preflight
   - Validate artifact signatures: sha256sum and registry image manifest.
   - Run smoke acceptance tests on staging cluster.
   - Publish upgrade plan, tenant grouping, and schedule to #private-deploy-upgrades and customer CS contacts.

2) T-24h: Freeze and final checks
   - Ensure backups exist: etcd snapshots, KV-store snapshot, model artifact snapshots.
   - Confirm rollback images are uploaded and tagged rollback-YYYYMMDD.

3) T-0: Canary launch
   - Deploy new images to canary namespace: kubectl apply -f canary-deployment.yaml
   - Redirect selected tenants via routing policy: rtrctl route set --tenant <id> --image <new-tag>
   - Start acceptance harness: ./acceptance-run --tenant <id> --suite canary-smoke

4) T+30–60m: Canary evaluation
   - Observe metrics: Grafana dashboard: PrivateDeploy/Canary/<release-id>
   - If all acceptance checks pass, get explicit approval from Release owner to proceed to phased rollout.

5) Phased rollout
   - Use the tenant-group schedule: 10% of tenants every 2 hours (or group boundaries as defined above)
   - Automate image promotion with tie-break gates: when automated checks pass, promote to next group; otherwise, pause and escalate.

6) Post-rollout verification
   - Run nightly full-traffic verification for 24h.
   - Run cumulative quality eval and publish report to release ticket.

Rollback mechanics (commands and verification)

- Instant rollback (image revert):
  - kubectl set image deployment/runtime runtime=registry.redwood-inference/private/runtime:<rollback-tag> -n <tenant-namespace>
  - Confirm pod turnover and readiness: kubectl rollout status deployment/runtime -n <tenant-namespace>
  - Re-run acceptance tests against the tenant to ensure baseline behavior restored.

- KV-store restore (if corruption detected):
  - Put service into maintenance mode: rtrctl tenant set-mode --tenant <id> maintenance
  - Restore snapshot: storagectl restore --snapshot <snapshot-id> --target <tenant-namespace>
  - Validate checksums and sample queries.

- Driver rollback (if applicable): follow vendor instructions and the Oncall Driver Rollback runbook; do not escalate to firmware-level rollbacks without Platform SRE approval.

Automated gating and telemetry

- Alerting thresholds (examples):
  - Canary API error rate > 0.5% -> PagerDuty P2 to SRE on-call
  - Canary 95th latency delta > +25% -> Slack alert and dashboard visual (no immediate Pd)
  - Any regression in model-quality eval -> Email to Applied ML + Product + Release owner

- Automation hooks:
  - CI pipeline posts to the release ticket with artifact digests and vulnerability scans.
  - A governance lambda checks preflight items and refuses rollout if critical checks fail.

Customer communication matrix

- Pre-announce (T-48h): maintenance window, risk assessment, and expected impact.
- Canary notify (T-0): which tenants are selected and how to opt-out if needed.
- Rollback/incident update cadence: every 30 minutes for P1, hourly for P2.

Runbook snippets and examples

Canary deployment YAML (simplified):
```
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: redwood-runtime
spec:
  replicas: 2
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: runtime
        image: registry.redwood-inference/private/runtime:new-release-20260915
        resources:
          limits:
            nvidia.com/gpu: 1
```

Acceptance command example:
```
./acceptance-run --tenant=acme-corp --suite=canary-smoke --report=reports/acme-canary-20260915.json
```

Escalation and decision points

- If canary fails any acceptance check, the Canary operator must pause and notify SRE within 10 minutes.
- SRE on-call has final authority to approve immediate rollback.
- If rollback is initiated, communicate to customers within 15 minutes and update the incident.

Metrics to capture for postmortem and continuous improvement

- Time-to-detect (median): target < 10 minutes
- Time-to-rollback decision (median): target < 20 minutes
- Time-to-recover (RTO) for typical rollbacks: target < 60 minutes
- Percentage of rollouts requiring manual rollback: target < 5% annually

Appendix: quick-reference checklist

- [ ] Artifact signed and stored
- [ ] Rollback image tagged and tested
- [ ] Backups and snapshots verified
- [ ] Canary tenants selected and notified
- [ ] Acceptance harness smoke passed
- [ ] Graph dashboards and alerts configured
- [ ] CS notified and customer comms prepared
